page: Vultr voc-m-8c-64gb-1600s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, the processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, and SHA_NI. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores align with the average tier. Memory performance is a notable strength, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidths ranking in the top 25%, alongside a strong PassMark memory score. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are average, while prompt processing for a medium 7B model is weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

The instance offers a balanced cost-efficiency profile for memory-intensive workloads, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local NVMe storage without the premium of specialized bare-metal hardware. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance, though the 2.0 GHz clock speed presents a tradeoff for single-threaded compute-bound tasks. This configuration is suitable for memory-optimized databases, caching layers, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications requiring local high-speed storage.
